Positions.Position Title: Data Production and Dissemination Development Officer
Key Activities: Develops processing systems and applications used to manipulate, store and retrieve statistical data.
Designs specifications for the testing of data and for the maintenance and development of databases.
Assesses changes in the subject area and determines the need to modify or replace processing systems and applications for the manipulation, storage and retrieval of statistical data
Provides subject matter advice and direction to users, negotiates procedural modifications and establishes project plans, priorities and target dates.
Participates as a subject area representative on teams and working groups throughout the department.
Leads project teams or supervises work units in the development and implementation of new or modified statistical processing systems.

1. Decision making: Identifies and assesses changes and developments in the subject area; determines the impact on program subject-matter content and the implication for statistical methods and procedures and the dissemination of program results.

Develops subject-matter concepts and definitions; proposes new statistical methods, techniques and approaches or the modification of existing techniques and approaches to improve program coverage or to meet specific needs.

Identifies and evaluates problems in the manipulation, storage and retrieval of statistical information to provide solutions or recommendations to management and to resolve subject-matter, conceptual and technical problems referred by staff.
Implements enhancements or modifications to processing systems and applications used to manipulate, store and retrieve statistical data.
2. Leadership and operational management: Leads project teams or work units. Determines goals, priorities and milestones, sets objectives, and plans and schedules the work, resolves conflicting priorities; assesses human resources needs, recommends the appropriate selection methods (internal and external resources / contractors) to meet program objectives, recruits staff, evaluates employee performance, develops training plans, motivates and maintains morale of employees.

Plans and budgets for special projects, including estimates for salaries, professional fees and implementation costs, with authority to allocate funds within budget. Provides input to budgets based on operational needs and by obtaining/providing cost estimates for personnel, supplies, equipment purchases and travel for use in developing section or division budgets. Procures goods and services within approved budget allocations.
3. Communication: Discusses program subject-matter content requirements with operations managers, other subject matter and systems specialists, clients, service providers and others to comprehend and elaborate the framework and conditions within which statistical development and operations will occur. There is a requirement to understand the issues and resolve differences that can affect the efficiency of the division's operations and quality of outputs.

Liaises with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development, to suggest improvements to ongoing programs, to negotiate procedural modifications and to establish project plans, priorities and target dates. Writes and presents detailed subject matter and technical concepts, definitions and terms in common terminology in order to explain and clarify divisional program content and applications.

Writes analytical reports and articles on the interpretation of surveys, statistical applications or project findings and the methodology used. These reports and articles are to be reviewed by program managers and included into publications. Exchanges information and provides advice to professionals from the private sector or from other statistical agencies abroad on subject-matter concepts and definitions, statistical survey methods and techniques. This information is used to develop similar surveys or analytical projects.

Provides guidance to other STC professionals on subject-matter concepts and definitions, survey methods, statistical applications and techniques used. This information is used to implement similar surveys or projects.
4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Knowledge of current or emerging economic and social issues relating to the program area in order to identify and resolve existing and potential subject-matter conflicts, duplication and gaps.

Knowledge of the concepts, methods and techniques used in the manipulation, storage and retrieval of statistical data in order to coordinate and advise on subject-matter development and resolve subject-matter concept and definition issues.

Knowledge of system analysis and design, computer processing, generalized survey software packages to manage the design, development, testing, maintenance and implementation of processing systems; to design specifications for the testing of data, and to maintain and develop databases.
Knowledge of high level programming languages, utility programs or statistical packages to retrieve and manipulate data.
Knowledge of management techniques and principles to manage financial and human resources, either directly or within a matrix management environment.
5. Contextual knowledge: Knowledge of statistical programs within Statistics Canada related to the area of expertise in order to identify and select sources of information for development and operations and/or special studies and to identify and evaluate data conflicts.

Knowledge of contacts within key client departments to establish a liaison; to understand need for statistical data, and to provide advice and guidance on subject-matter concepts, methods, techniques and results.
Knowledge of the divisional mandate, objectives, priorities, practices, standards, processes and procedures in order to coordinate and manage on-going operational activities and/or special projects.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act and other pertinent acts such as the Corporate Returns Act and Income Tax Act, and of Statistics Canada policies to explain legislative and policy requirements to data suppliers, users and others with respect to the manipulation, storage and retrieval of data. Knowledge of the Statistics and Privacy Acts is particulary important with respect to the security and confidentiality of information and data provided and to ensure that they and their subordinates do not release any information which may identify an individual or group without prior consent.
6. Research and analysis: Plans and implements the review and development of new subject-matter methods, concepts and definitions and conducts studies and analytical projects to improve existing surveys and data.

Analyzes current manipulation, storage and retrieval methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to determine the need for modification or replacement with alternative systems, methods and procedures.

Conducts feasibility studies concerning new system and product requirements by examining existing, proposed or new software programs and systems to determine their feasibility and adaptability to the needs of the statistical program.

Provides subject-matter interpretation and analysis to media representatives on the results of surveys or projects, and the interpretation of statistical data. This information is disseminated to the Canadian population for information and decision making purposes.

Education: Successful completion of two years of a post secondary program with acceptable specialization in social science, statistics, library/archival work or a law related field.
An acceptable combination of education, training and/or experience.
Experience: Experience in development/implementation of data processing or software specifications.
Experience in testing of survey processes/applications.
Experience in editing, processing, or integration of data.
Experience in validation and confrontation of data.
Experience in preparation of data for dissemination.
Experience in data manipulation using software such as SAS, Python, R, SQL, Stata, SPSS, C++, Java, Visual Basic.
Competencies: Showing initiative and being action oriented
Abilities: Ability to use reasoning skills to solve problems
Ability to communicate effectively in writing.
Assets: Experience working with the Census Response Data Base
